programs.title: Tactical FPS foundation
programs.summary: Interaction, inventory, weapon wear, and replication. You study the pieces, then load a starter project you can build on.

steps.title: Look with a timer

predict.prompt: When should this foundation look for an actor?
choices: On a timer, about ten times a second.
predict.why: A timer sleeps between looks. Tick would keep tracing while you stand still.

steps.why: A timer sleeps between looks. Tick would keep tracing while you stand still.

steps.title: One interface

predict.prompt: How does interact reach a door and a dropped weapon?
choices: The graph casts to each Blueprint.
predict.why: A cast chain grows every time you add something the player can use.

steps.why: A cast chain grows every time you add something the player can use.
steps.task: What does the component call instead of a cast?

steps.title: Two functions

predict.prompt: The event graph traces and interacts in one chain. What should you do with it?
choices: Collapse it into two functions, one for the trace and one for the interact.
Leave it as one long chain so the order stays obvious.
Move both into Tick so they stay in sync.
predict.why: A function has one job. The event graph should call Trace, then call Interact. A macro would paste the same nodes back into every caller.

steps.why: A function has one job. The event graph should call Trace, then call Interact. A macro would paste the same nodes back into every caller.
steps.task: Open the starter in Tools and collapse the trace and the interact into two functions. Then check.

steps.title: The stack lives on the item

predict.prompt: Where does the max stack live?
choices: On a new inventory subclass for each item.
predict.why: The widget draws slots. It does not own the rule, or the next item drifts.

steps.why: The widget draws slots. It does not own the rule, or the next item drifts.
steps.task: Type the kind of asset the stack size is read from.

steps.title: Replicate the wear, not the mesh

predict.prompt: What should replicate when the gun wears?
choices: Nothing. Each client wears its own gun.
predict.why: The mesh is already on the weapon. Other machines need the number, then they play the scuff.

steps.why: The mesh is already on the weapon. Other machines need the number, then they play the scuff.
steps.task: Type the name of the value that replicates.

steps.title: The server owns the change

predict.prompt: A client presses fire and something loses health. Where does the damage run?
choices: On the client that pressed fire.
predict.why: The client can ask. The server decides the health that everyone else sees.

steps.why: The client can ask. The server decides the health that everyone else sees.
steps.task: Type where ApplyDamage is allowed to change health.

compares.title: Blueprint actor or C++ component
compares.note: The foundation uses a component. Any pawn can gain interaction without a new character class.

left.label: Blueprint actor
left.body:
A new BP_Interactor is placed in the level.
The character casts to it to trace.
A second character needs a second actor, or a child of the first character.

right.label: C++ component
right.body:
UTacticalInteractComponent sits on the pawn.
BeginPlay starts the timer.
The character does not subclass for this, and the door only implements the interface.

compares.title: Tick or an event
compares.feature: How the look check and the prompt run
compares.note: The foundation uses a timer for the trace and a delegate for the prompt. Tick stays off.

left.label: Tick
left.body:
TickComponent calls TraceForFocus every frame.
The widget also reads FocusedActor on Tick.
Both keep running while the player stands still.

right.label: Event-driven
right.body:
BeginPlay sets a timer for TraceForFocus.
OnFocusChanged.Broadcast tells the prompt.
Tick is left off.

nodes.title: Input
nodes.detail: The key press calls Try Interact. It does not trace, and it does not change health.

nodes.title: Interaction
nodes.detail: A timer traces 500 cm from the camera, ignores the player, and calls the interface on the authority.

nodes.title: Health
nodes.detail: ApplyDamage runs on the authority. Health replicates with OnRep so the UI can play the hit.

nodes.title: UI
nodes.detail: The prompt and the health readout listen to events. They do not tick, and they do not decide the rules.

nodes.title: Inventory
nodes.detail: AddItem reads MaxStack from the item data. The widget only draws what the component already stored.

nodes.title: Weapon wear
nodes.detail: AddWear changes a replicated float. The mesh stays on the weapon.

starter.summary: Interaction, inventory, weapon wear, and health for a blank UE 5.8 C++ project. The same code builds on 5.7. Tick stays off.

modules.name: Interaction
modules.description: Timer trace, ignore the player, interface call on the authority.

modules.name: Weapon Wear
modules.description: A replicated wear float with OnRep. The mesh is not replicated.

starter.blueprint_pseudocode:
Event BeginPlay
  Set Timer (Trace For Focus, Trace Interval, looping)
WHY: Tick stays off. The timer is enough for a look prompt.

Function Trace For Focus
  Line trace from the camera by Trace Distance
  Ignore the player
  If the hit implements Interact, set Focus and broadcast
WHY: The prompt listens. It does not poll.

Function Try Interact
  If no authority, Server Try Interact
  Else call Interact on the focused actor
WHY: The interface runs where the server can see it.

Function Add Item
  Read Max Stack from the item data
  Reject the add when the stack is full
WHY: The widget does not own the number.

Function Add Wear
  If authority, add Wear Per Shot and replicate Wear
WHY: OnRep plays the scuff. The mesh stays put.

Function Apply Damage
  If authority, subtract from Health
WHY: A client asking is not the same as the client deciding.

setup_guide.title: Drop the two files into your game module
setup_guide.detail: Put TacticalFPSFoundation.h and .cpp in Source/<YourGame>. A blank C++ project already depends on Engine.
setup_guide.why: No extra plugin is required. The code stays on Engine types that 5.7 and 5.8 share.

setup_guide.title: Add the components to the character
setup_guide.detail: Add interaction, inventory, weapon wear, and health to the player character.
setup_guide.why: The character does not subclass for each system.

setup_guide.title: Implement the interface on usable actors
setup_guide.why: One call covers the next usable actor.

setup_guide.title: Bind the prompt to On Focus Changed
setup_guide.detail: The widget shows while focus is set.
setup_guide.why: The UI listens. It does not tick.

starter.network_notes: Focus stays local. Interact, wear, and health change on the authority and replicate with OnRep. Built for a blank UE 5.8 C++ project and the same code on 5.7.

courses.title: Tactical FPS, first course
courses.summary: Four short modules. A quiz, a diff, a practical line, and a takeaway in each one.

modules.title: Looking at the world
modules.takeaway: Trace from the camera on a timer, far enough to reach a doorway, and skip the player who is looking.

assignment.prompt: In one line, say how far the trace is and that it ignores the player.

quiz.why: Tick would run while the player stands still.
quiz.review_prompt: How is the look check scheduled?

quiz.prompt: How far is the foundation trace?
quiz.why: 500 cm reaches a door without scanning the map.
quiz.review_prompt: What distance does this course use for the look trace?

quiz.prompt: Should the trace hit the player holding the camera?
choices: Yes. The player is a valid target.
quiz.why: Ignoring the owner stops the prompt sticking to your own capsule.
quiz.review_prompt: Does the foundation trace include the owner?

diff.review_prompt: One of these look checks is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: The right-hand check runs every frame and can hit the player.

right.label: Tick, player included
right.code:
void Tick() { TraceForFocus(); }
// owner is a valid hit

modules.title: What the player carries
modules.takeaway: The item data owns the stack size. The widget only draws the slots the component already decided.

assignment.prompt: Name where Max Stack lives, in a few words.

quiz.prompt: Where does the max stack live?
quiz.why: A number in the click drifts from the next item.

quiz.review_prompt: The inventory widget's job is to do what?

quiz.why: A local add desyncs the other machines.
quiz.review_prompt: An item add has to run where?

diff.review_prompt: One stack rule is in the wrong place. Which side?
diff.why: Hardcoding 99 in the click ignores the item data.

modules.title: Wear and replication
modules.takeaway: Replicate the wear value. OnRep plays the scuff. Leave the mesh where it is.

assignment.prompt: Name the replicated value and the function that runs when it arrives.

quiz.prompt: What replicates when the gun wears?
choices: The whole weapon actor, every frame.
quiz.why: Clients need the number, not a second mesh.
quiz.review_prompt: Which property should the wear system replicate?

choices: To play the local reaction after the value arrives.
quiz.why: OnRep runs on the machines that received the new value.
quiz.review_prompt: After wear replicates, which function should react?

quiz.why: The mesh is already on the weapon.
quiz.review_prompt: Does the wear system replicate the mesh?

diff.review_prompt: One of these replication lines is the wrong property. Which side?
diff.why: Replicating the mesh shares a pointer. Wear is the value that changed.

modules.title: How the systems connect
modules.takeaway: Input asks. Interaction decides. Health and inventory change on the authority. UI listens.

assignment.prompt: Say what input calls, and how the prompt hears about focus.

quiz.why: Input is a request. The interaction component does the trace.
quiz.review_prompt: The interact key should call which function?

choices: It binds to On Focus Changed.
quiz.why: The event fires when focus actually changes.
quiz.review_prompt: The prompt should update by doing what?

quiz.why: The UI shows health. It does not subtract it.
quiz.review_prompt: Health is allowed to change where?

diff.review_prompt: One prompt update is the broken one. Which side?
diff.why: Reading focus on Tick keeps the widget awake and hides the moment focus changed.
